claims.answer: Desktop editor on Windows (64-bit), macOS and Linux with the Chat view; Agents window on desktop and in a browser at vscode.dev/agents (needs GitHub sign-in and a registered host or dev tunnel); code CLI with code chat and code --agents; no VS Code mobile app, but a phone-width browser layout exists and GitHub Mobile can continue sessions registered as GitHub environments.

mobile_apps.answer: No VS Code mobile app is documented; the Agent Host documentation says GitHub Mobile can continue sessions of registered GitHub environments, but that is a separate GitHub client.

mobile_browser.answer: The browser Agents window has a phone layout (host picker in the title bar of the new-session screen) built on shared Sessions services.

cli.answer: code CLI provides code chat, code --agents, code tunnel, serve-web and an agent subcommand for agent host sessions.

editor_extensions.answer: VS Code is itself the editor; Copilot Chat and other agent integrations are extensions (OpenAI Codex extension, Copilot Chat) installable from the Marketplace.

task_actions.answer: Start, steer (Add to Queue or Steer with Message), approve, review changes and resume sessions from the Chat view and Agents window; browser client can continue a task and start a new one.

notifications.answer: Sessions list shows unread and in-progress badges and Inbox mode groups items needing attention; OS-level push notification behavior is not documented in the pages checked.

cross_device_continuity.answer: GitHub environments, SSH and dev tunnels let other machines reopen a session that keeps running on its host; cloud sessions can be reopened from another client.

limitations: No native VS Code iOS or Android app; phone access is the browser Agents window or the separate GitHub Mobile client for GitHub environments.
Browser Agents window requires GitHub sign-in and cannot connect directly over SSH.
Cloud sessions, GitHub environments and some harness integrations are feature-gated or experimental.

claims.answer: Embeds the Copilot harness (Copilot SDK) in an Agent Host process and also runs Claude (Claude Agent SDK) and Codex harnesses (Codex via extension or experimental Agent Host); a deprecated Local harness is removed by February 2027; models come from Copilot, BYOK providers, model provider extensions and on-device models; mixed-harness chats group different harnesses in one session.

harnesses.answer: Copilot, Claude and Codex harnesses plus the deprecated Local harness are listed; Cloud is an execution target for the Copilot harness.

model_providers.answer: Models through Copilot (multiple providers), BYOK providers, model provider extensions such as Ollama and Copilot-managed on-device MAI Code 1.1 Flash.

custom_adapters.answer: Agent adapters plug into the Agent Host through the open Agent Host Protocol and extensions can contribute chat sessions, tools and custom agents; third-party harness adapters are not documented as a user-configurable list.

session_integration.answer: Harnesses run embedded in the Agent Host (Copilot SDK, Claude Agent SDK) with sessions owned by the host; the Codex extension runs through its own integration.

mixed_harness_operation.answer: Mixed-harness chats start separate conversations on different harnesses inside one session (feature-gated).

limitations: The Claude harness is enabled by default unless enterprise-managed settings disable it, but using it without GitHub sign-in is experimental; the Codex Agent Host integration, Agent Host BYOK and mixed-harness chats are experimental, and Claude and Codex are disabled under enterprise-managed settings.
Local harness is deprecated and documented as removed by February 2027.

claims.answer: GitHub Copilot subscription (Free, Pro, Pro+ and organizational plans) with AI credits; Claude via Copilot-routed models or a Claude API key / supported provider config; Codex via Copilot Pro+ or a ChatGPT account (a free ChatGPT account suffices); BYOK for chat in Local and (experimentally) Copilot harness sessions; Ollama and on-device models work locally.
